newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to float up to 26 pct of KGHM in London.
newsitem.headline: Poland to float up to 26 pct of KGHM in London.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday gave a final go-ahead for the privatisation of the KGHM Polska Miedz SA copper concern and decided to float up to 26 percent of it in London, the government said in a statement.

"The government authorised the treasury ministry to sell a selected depositary bank no more than 26 percent of the state treasury's shares in the company, which will allow to issue...Global Depositary Receipts," the statement said.
It said the offering would lead to a first ever full listing of Polish company's GDRs on the London Stock Exchange.
"This decision confirms the Polish government's commitment to the privatisation programme. It should lead to improving Poland's position on international capital markets," the statement said.
It said that, under a new privatisation law that came into force on April 8, up to 15 percent of KGHM would be offered to the copper firm's employees for free.
Senior government officials earlier said KGHM's privatisation plan also envisaged floating the coppper firm's shares on the Warsaw bourse, but the statement did not refer to the domestic offering.
Last week Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz told Reuters that part of KGHM shares would be earmarked to help finance Poland's crucial reform of the social security system.
Under a preliminary plan, the government would issue bonds convertible into shares of companies undergoing privatisation to finance the creation of new, independent pension funds.
Revenues from the sell-off of the company estimated to be worth a total of $2-3 billion are also expected to help meet budget revenues targets this year.
"A succesfull sale of KHGM will significantly affect the implementation of the 1997 budget," the statement said.

Government officials were not immediately available for comment. Last year KGHM earned netted 147.2 million zlotys on sales of 3.59 billion zlotys, down from 481.9 million and 3.72 billion respectively in 1995.
